critiques.assumption: A shared partition mapping makes workshop completeness and customer guidance jointly more reliable.
critiques.limitation: A wrong overlay could populate mat and slip consistently, producing a complete-looking kit for the wrong arrangement. D2-O1 establishes count and color variation, but no observation establishes this mapping failure. Z2 verifies contents without establishing affordable operational verification.
critiques.opening: Reconcile the shared mapping against the accepted order independently before using it for both staging and instructions.
critiques.comparison: Z1 organizes selection; Z2 clarifies destination; A1 links occupancy checking and destination guidance. Their interaction can propagate incorrect mappings. Reconciliation could intercept those errors but adds time and requires an authoritative order description.
critiques.probe: Proposed, unperformed: introduce recoverable wrong-layout overlays and examine whether ordinary A1 checking versus independent reconciliation catches them. Seeded results establish detection capability only, not natural error frequency.

openings.claim: Combine A1 linked aids with a separate accepted-order reconciliation before kit release.
openings.delta: Distinguish agreement between aids from correctness against the customer order; do not derive the independent check from the same overlay.
openings.prediction: Relative to mat alone, the slip should reduce destination confusion; relative to slip alone, the mat should improve omission detection. Relative to A1, reconciliation should catch more shared mapping errors. No time advantage is assumed.
openings.probe: Proposed, unperformed: smallest capability is independently recovering ordered layout, count and color and detecting a mismatched overlay. If feasible, reuse at most 15 sample sets across mat-only, slip-only, linked and reconciled-linked conditions; counterbalance workers. Include all preparation and checking in assembly/packing time. Use ten participants for exploratory first-use comparisons; assess original success thresholds in the 60-order pilot.
openings.fit: Preserves footprint, assortment, removable partitions, accepted counts and colors. Adoption remains conditional on both cost caps, fixed delivery date and the original performance targets.
assumptions: Accepted-order information independently specifies the intended arrangement.
Reconciliation does not merely repeat the overlay error.
Preparation and checking fit available working time; insertion difficulties remain unresolved.
